title: Chapter 38 — Price, Discount, and Competitor Quote Objections
intro: Discount discipline, the competitor quote on the counter, and negotiating without eroding trust or margin.

sections.title: The Discount Trap
sections.content:
Discounting is the easiest and worst habit in sales. It is easy because it makes the problem go away — temporarily. It is the worst because it trains customers to always negotiate and it trains you to sell on price instead of value.

Only 21% of appliance shoppers even negotiate. Which means 79% of your customers are not asking for a discount. If you offer one to every customer, you are giving away margin to people who never asked for it.

sections.title: When the Competitor Quote Appears
sections.content:
A customer puts a quote from your competitor on the counter. 'Can you beat this?'

Before you react, do three things. First, verify the quote is real and complete — does it include delivery, installation, warranty, and the same model? Second, compare complete tickets. Third, articulate what you offer that the competitor does not.

Sometimes the competitor's quote is genuinely better. In that case, match it if your policy allows — but only after you have demonstrated your value. Sometimes the competitor's quote is missing components. In that case, show the customer the real comparison.

sections.title: Negotiate Without Eroding Trust
sections.content:
If you do need to negotiate, do it professionally. Never make the customer feel like the first price was a lie.

'I want to earn your business. Let me see what I can do on the total package.' That is honest. It tells the customer you are working for them.

'Fine, I will knock off $200.' That feels like the price was inflated to begin with. It erodes trust even while closing the sale.

The way you negotiate matters as much as the number you land on.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating discount and competitor objections, ask:

Does the salesperson lead with value — or jump straight to discounting?
Do they verify competitor quotes before reacting?
Do they compare complete tickets — or just product prices?
Do they negotiate professionally — or make the customer feel like the original price was dishonest?
Do they use price matching strategically — or give it away reflexively?

Selling value creates repeat customers. Selling discounts creates bargain hunters.
